page.layout: Two blocks: running text in one column (main text, right of centre), with marginal notes in the left margin beside the first lines of the page. The top carries the page number and running head. No notes below the text; the page ends with a signature line for "FRANCISCVS ZABARELLA" and continues on the next page.

main_text.p: praescriptum imperiumque ejus, qui mandavit, agat: Legato ca-vēda πτρ- πσεσβεια. à χαὶ vero, & falsa legatione summopere abhorreat: utpote quae cum perfidia utplurimum conjunêta est: qua nulla Aleêto nec furia infernalis perniciosior: quae perfido non tantum dedecus, sed perniciem quoque affert. Ecquis enim non exsecretur Dositheï perfidiam? qui ab Hyrcano, Herodis Regis socero, missus cum literis ad Malchum Regem Arabum, quibus Hyrcanus fugam meditabatur; literas eas Herodi tradidit: & hujus consilio denuò obsignatas ad Malchum detulit: cumque Malchus Hyrcano opem polliceretur, hujus quoque literas Herodi oftendit: qui mox Hyrcanum focerum, annum agentem octogesimum, interficiendum curavit: teste Josepho lib.15.Antiqq.cap.9. Quis non improbaret nefarii istius Spadonis perfidiam: qui ab Alexio Angelo Byzantino Imperatore, à quo Ibancus defecerat, & loca monti Haemo finitima firmis castellis munierat, ad hunc reconciliandum missus; & ut pacta simul atque conventa, insuperque neptis suae nuptias in memoriam ei revocaret: non modo nihil, quod ad rem pertineret, confecit: sed illum quoque sua praesentia, ut coepta perseque retur, magis confirmavit: cum temerè effutissel, Graecos eveftigio illum invasuros: & monuisset, ut campestribus relictis suam & popularium salutem montanis locis committeret. Nicetas lib.3. de imperio Alexii.

Magis vero detestanda CONSTANTINI Diogenis perfidia: qui à Constantino Imperatore ad Sermonem Sirmii dominum legatus missus; interposito jurejurando affirmavit, cupere se ipsum convenire, ac de rebus necessariis colloqui: quod si ipse insidias vereretur, tribus tantum famulis stipatum se ad ripam profluentis ibi amnis accessurum: idem tamen ipse quoque faceret. Ibi ergo cum jam collocuturi essent: Diogenes pugionem, quem in finu abditum gestabat, subito in latus Sermonis adegit, eumque occidit: ut Cedrenus scribit.

page.notes: Left-margin notes read as Greek and Latin reference marks: the first "Legato ca-" and "vēda" lines and the Greek word beside them are partly garbled in the scan; the Greek "πτρ" and "πσεσβεια" are uncertain. Marginal "3942." appears beside the Hyrcanus paragraph and is a page-side number, not text. The Greek word after "à" is illegible; "χ" is a best guess. Several words are uncertain in the scan (e.g. "Ibancus", "Byzantino", "Diogenis") and should be checked against the original. Final line is cut off at the bottom; "cujus" continues on the next page.
